title: (fix) O3-6055: Default publish-only input to false for CI events
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [[conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines)](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [[Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)](http://om.rs/o3ui)) — Not applicable; CI configuration only.
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. — Validated using YAML parsing and GitHub’s expression library, as described below.

## Summary

Fix the CI input validation error introduced by the one-click release changes merged in #755.

On push and pull-request events, `inputs.publish_only` is absent and evaluates to an empty value. The shared release workflow requires a boolean, so GitHub rejects the input with `Unexpected value ''`.

Update the mapping to:

```yaml
publish_only: ${{ inputs.publish_only || false }}
```

This supplies boolean `false` when the input is absent and preserves the selected checkbox value for manual runs.

The PR contains one commit changing one line, based on the current OpenMRS `main`.

## Screenshots

Not applicable; no UI changes.

## Related Issue

[[O3-6055: Add one-click release inputs to CI in openmrs-esm-cohortbuilder-app](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6055)](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6055)

Follow-up to #755.

## Other

Validation completed:

- GitHub’s `@actions/expressions` library reproduces the original empty-value problem.
- Expression checks confirm boolean `false` for absent or unchecked inputs and boolean `true` for checked inputs.
- YAML parsing succeeds.
- Comparison against current `main` confirms only the `publish_only` mapping changes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

No real release was triggered. GitHub CI remains to be verified on this PR.

title: (chore) O3-6055: Enable one-click releases
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [[conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines)](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [[Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - Not applicable; CI configuration changes only.
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. - Validated through YAML parsing and configuration checks described below.

## Summary

Enable one-click releases through the **Run workflow** action in OpenMRS CI.

- Add `release_type`, `custom_version`, and `publish_only` inputs with the descriptions, types, and defaults specified in the ticket.
- Pass the inputs to the shared release workflow, mapping `custom_version` to `release_version`.
- Remove the old `release: created` trigger to prevent duplicate publishing.
- Add `.github/release.yml` to exclude `openmrs-bot` from generated release notes.
- Remove the release job condition that blocked manual runs.

## Screenshots

Not applicable; no UI changes.

## Related Issue

[[O3-6055: Add one-click release inputs to CI in openmrs-esm-cohortbuilder-app](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6055)](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-6055)

## Other

The ticket asks to preserve existing job conditions. However, the existing condition, `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'`, explicitly skips manual runs. Keeping it would allow **Run workflow** to build the application but skip the release job. It was therefore removed to enable the intended one-click release flow.

Validation completed:

- Both YAML files parse successfully.
- Configuration checks verify the inputs, mappings, removed trigger and condition, and bot exclusion.
- Comparison with the original workflow confirms all unrelated configuration remains unchanged.
- `git diff --check` passes.

No real release was triggered. A maintainer should perform the first release after merge.

title: (fix) Renumber every filter when composing search history items
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
When a composition like `1 AND 2` pulls in a history item, that item's filter numbers need to shift by the number of filters already in the composed query. `formatFilterCombination` used `/\d/` without the global flag, so only the first single digit moved. A history item with `1 AND 2 AND NOT 3` added after one existing filter was sent as `2 AND 2 AND NOT 3` instead of `2 AND 3 AND NOT 4`. Reporting accepts that and quietly evaluates the wrong cohort.

Match every number with `/\d+/g`, which also handles filter numbers above 9.

title: (fix) Load translations under the app's package name
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary
The lifecycle options named the module `@openmrs/esm-cohort-builder`, but the package is `@openmrs/esm-cohort-builder-app`. The app shell resolves translation namespaces through the import map, so every page logged `Could not find the package @openmrs/esm-cohort-builder defined in the current importmap` and the app's translations (and any configured overrides) never loaded. The UI only read correctly because every `t()` call has an English default.

This fixes the module name. Since `en.json` now actually loads, it also fixes the entries that were exported with the key as their value (`deleteCohort`, `error`, `saving`, etc.) and gives the Saved Cohorts and Saved Queries tabs separate keys. They shared `savedDefinitions`, which would have labelled both tabs "Saved Definitions".

## Screenshots


## Related Issue

## Other
We only ship `en.json` today, so the user-visible effect right now is the console error and config overrides starting to work. This mostly matters once translations land from Transifex.

See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

This PR replaces `jwalton/gh-docker-logs` in the E2E workflow with the org's shared [`capture-docker-logs`](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows/blob/main/.github/actions/capture-docker-logs/action.yml) action from [openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows#60](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-contrib-gha-workflows/pull/60). It does the same thing: it writes each container's logs to `logs/<container name>.log` for the upload step that follows.

`jwalton/gh-docker-logs` declares the Node 20 runtime, which GitHub [removed from hosted runners](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/) on September 23. Runners now force it onto Node 24 with a deprecation warning. It hasn't had a release since v2.2.2 in January 2024, so there's no Node 24 version to upgrade to.

Same change as [openmrs-esm-core#1928](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-core/pull/1928).

title: (chore) Share SWR through module federation
body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [ ] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Adds `swr` to `peerDependencies` so the build tooling federates it, and pins the exact `2.5.1` devDependency so the fallback copy matches the app shell.

The openmrs rspack config builds the module federation `shared` list from `peerDependencies`. `swr` was only reaching this app transitively, so the built entry registered no `swr` share and bundled a private copy. `useSWR` from that copy reads its own `SWRConfig` context, not the one the framework's component decorator provides, so the cohort builder has been running on SWR's stock defaults (revalidate on focus and reconnect, unlimited retries on every error) and its own cache rather than the shared one.

Verified by building and checking the remote entry, which now registers `swr`, `swr/_internal`, `swr/immutable` and `swr/infinite` at 2.5.1 like the other O3 apps. Same change as openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-builder#1347, where the dev server run against dev3 showed the forms list stop refetching on window focus once the framework's `revalidateOnFocus: false` applied.

## Screenshots

## Related Issue

## Other

Reports and laboratory have the same gap. Separate PRs to follow.

body:
## Requirements

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/en-US/docs/frontend-modules/contributing/#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Since openmrs/openmrs-distro-referenceapplication#1062, the nightly frontend image ships precompressed `importmap.json` and `routes.registry.json`, and its nginx config serves the `.br`/`.gz` variants before the plain files. The e2e image kept the stale compressed importmap from the nightly image, which points at versioned app directories that the glob `COPY` flattens, so e2e runs time out waiting for the shell to load. This broke e2e CI in several O3 repos starting 2026-08-21.

This copies the frontend files with their directory structure intact and removes the stale compressed variants, so the freshly assembled importmap and routes registry are the ones served. Same fix as openmrs/openmrs-esm-patient-management#2687.

## Summary

This moves the repository from its legacy eslintrc setup and ESLint 8 to `@openmrs/eslint-config` and ESLint 9. The flat config preserves the existing repo-specific, type-aware, test, and Playwright rules while removing the redundant direct plugin dependencies.

The dependency updater now names only the packages that actually publish a `next` tag, so it leaves the stable-only ESLint config on its declared range.

ESLint 9 also caught a side-effect-only ternary in the concept search component. This replaces it with the equivalent `if` statement.

- [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration.
- [x] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui))
- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Migrates cohortbuilder-app's test runner from jest to vitest, aligning it with the patterns adopted across the rest of the O3 apps.

Changes:
- Replace `jest`, `@swc/jest`, `jest-cli`, `jest-environment-jsdom`, and `@types/jest` with `vitest`, `@vitest/coverage-v8`, `jsdom`, and `cross-env`. Bump `@testing-library/dom` (8.x to 10.x), `@testing-library/jest-dom` (5.x to 6.x), and `@testing-library/react` (13.x to 16.x) so the `/vitest` subpath is available.
- Add `vitest.config.ts`: `jsdom` environment, `.scss`/`.css` aliased to `identity-obj-proxy` via the anchored `^.*\.s?css$` regex, `@openmrs/esm-framework` aliased to its mock, `react-i18next` aliased to the local `__mocks__` file (the local mock provides a `defaultValue` fallback that the bare `react-i18next` mock from the framework does not, which several tests rely on for translation assertions), and `fakeTimers.toFake` limited so it does not break React's scheduler.
- Update `tools/setup-tests.ts` to load `@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest`, register `afterEach(cleanup)`, and swap `jest.fn` for `vi.fn` in the `window.matchMedia` mock. Delete the now-unused `src/setup-tests.ts` (the jest config only referenced `tools/setup-tests.ts`).
- Convert the seventeen test files to the vitest API: explicit imports for `describe`/`expect`/`it`/`vi` (plus `type Mock` and `beforeEach` where used), `jest.*` swapped for `vi.*`. The eight `jest.mock(name, () => { const original = jest.requireActual(name); ... })` factories rewritten as the async `vi.mock(name, async (importOriginal) => { const original = await importOriginal<typeof Mod>(); ... })` form, importing the target module type alias via `import type * as ...` so the eslint `consistent-type-imports` rule stays happy.
- Delete `jest.config.js`.


## Screenshots

N/A — tooling change only.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Other

All 26 tests pass locally. \`yarn lint\` and \`yarn typescript\` are green.

- [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests.

## Summary

Switch the bundler from webpack to rspack, matching the migration already landed across the rest of the distro.

- Rename `webpack.config.js` → `rspack.config.js` and require `openmrs/default-rspack-config`
- Update `package.json` `build` / `serve` / `analyze` scripts to call `rspack`
- Drop `@types/webpack-env` and declare `RequireContext` + `NodeJS.Require` locally in `src/declarations.d.ts` so `require.context` still type-checks

## Screenshots

N/A — build tooling only.

## Related Issue

N/A.

## Other

Verified locally with `yarn build`, `yarn typescript`, and `yarn lint` — all green.
